readme: Sampled-frame replays derived from saved local observations; no new inference. Frame indices are stored sample indices, not wall-clock timestamps. v2 progress uses current and past frames; first score is initialized to zero.

cases.title: The right object, placed and released
cases.summary: The blue cup is lifted into the sink and released. The final progress estimate reaches 1.00.
cases.protocol: v2 causal autoregressive progress; first value fixed at zero
cases.relationToReport: Supplementary qualitative case from existing evaluation records; not a new benchmark result
cases.playbackNote: 32 stored frames replayed at 4 fps. Display time is not original execution time.
reasons: Initial reference observation; progress is defined as zero.
The gripper has descended toward a position above the blue cup, making an initial approach. The cup remains on the counter and has not yet been grasped or moved toward the sink.

The gripper has descended into contact with the blue cup at its rim, advancing from the earlier approach to grasp positioning. The cup remains on the counter; lifting and moving it into the sink are still required.
The gripper has lifted the blue cup off the counter and carried it to the sink's left edge. The cup remains suspended outside the basin and still needs to be placed inside.
The blue cup is now upright inside the sink basin, and the gripper has withdrawn above it. The instructed placement is complete.
cases.evidenceNote: Official quality is a trajectory label. Progress estimates are model outputs, not human annotated completion percentages. Cases were selected after evaluation.

cases.title: A transfer can lose progress
cases.summary: The cup moves toward the sink but ends outside the basin. The estimate falls from 0.55 to 0.40.
cases.protocol: v2 causal autoregressive progress; first value fixed at zero
cases.relationToReport: Supplementary qualitative case from existing evaluation records; not a new benchmark result
cases.playbackNote: 32 stored frames replayed at 4 fps. Display time is not original execution time.
reasons: Initial reference observation; progress is defined as zero.
The gripper has lowered toward the cup's vicinity, improving its approach position. The blue cup remains on the counter, with no visible grasp or movement toward the sink yet.
The gripper has reached the blue cup and lowered its fingers into and around the rim, positioning for a grasp. The cup remains on the counter; lifting and moving it into the sink are still required.
The gripper has lifted the blue cup and moved it toward the sink, holding it near the sink's left edge. The cup is still outside the basin and must be placed inside.
The cup has moved next to the sink but appears to have slipped from the gripper and is tilted outside the basin. It is closer to the destination, but must be grasped again and placed inside.

cases.title: Motion is not task progress
cases.summary: The robot moves a white cup instead of the requested blue cup. The estimate returns to zero.
cases.protocol: v2 causal autoregressive progress; first value fixed at zero
cases.relationToReport: Supplementary qualitative case from existing evaluation records; not a new benchmark result
cases.playbackNote: 32 stored frames replayed at 4 fps. Display time is not original execution time.
reasons: Initial reference observation; progress is defined as zero.
The gripper has lowered toward the work area but is currently above the red plate, to the right of the blue cup. The cup remains unmoved on the counter and has not been grasped or placed in the sink.
The gripper is lowered beside the blue cup, but no grasp or displacement of the cup is visible. The cup remains on the counter outside the sink.

The gripper has lifted the small pale object rather than the blue cup and moved away from the cup. The blue cup remains at its initial position on the counter, with no task-relevant placement progress.
The robot has moved the pale object into the sink, not the blue cup. The blue cup remains unmoved at its initial position on the counter.

cases.title: A failed approach, then a successful retry
cases.task: Pick up the banana from the blue plate and place it on the green plate
cases.summary: The robot withdraws with the banana still on the blue plate, approaches again, and ultimately transfers it to the green plate.
cases.protocol: v2 causal autoregressive progress; first value fixed at zero
cases.relationToReport: Supplementary qualitative case from existing evaluation records; not a new benchmark result
cases.playbackNote: 32 stored frames replayed at 4 fps. Display time is not original execution time.
reasons: Initial reference observation; progress is defined as zero.
The gripper is positioned close above the banana, but the banana remains on the blue plate after the plate was disturbed. No secure pickup or transfer to the empty green plate is visible.
The arm has withdrawn from the blue plate, losing the earlier close grasping position. The banana remains on the blue plate and the green plate is empty; no pickup or transfer has been achieved.
The gripper has returned to the banana at the blue plate's edge, providing a close pickup position. The banana is not visibly lifted clear of the plate, and the green plate remains empty.
The banana is now resting on the green plate, and the gripper has lifted away. The banana is no longer on the blue plate, completing the requested transfer.

cases.title: Higher correlation, worse endpoint judgment
cases.summary: The public terminal label is success. Adding a single-trajectory example raises time correlation while lowering the final completion estimate from 1.00 to 0.35. The visual completion state is not independently adjudicated.
cases.protocol: v2 causal autoregressive progress; first value fixed at zero
cases.playbackNote: 32 stored frames replayed at 4 fps. Display time is not original execution time.
reasons: Initial reference observation; progress is defined as zero.
The gripper has moved toward the bottle and is positioned with open fingers just above its cap. The cap remains attached, with no visible grasp or opening yet.
The gripper has descended and is positioned closely around the bottle's capped neck, improving engagement for opening. The white cap remains seated, with no visible loosening or removal.
The foreground jaws have closed in around the bottle, improving stabilization while the upper gripper remains near the capped neck. The cap is still seated, with no visible loosening or removal.
The bottle has tilted away from the white cap, exposing its threaded neck behind the cap. The cap is separated from the mouth, achieving the opening goal.

reasons: Initial reference observation; progress is defined as zero.
The gripper has moved down toward the bottle and is positioned just above its cap, providing an approach toward grasping it. The cap remains attached, with no visible loosening or opening yet.
The gripper has descended to closely flank the bottle cap, improving its positioning for a grasp. The cap remains seated on the bottle, with no visible loosening or removal.

The foreground jaws have closed around the bottle body, providing stabilization while the upper gripper remains positioned near the cap. The cap is still seated, with no visible separation or opening.

The bottle remains braced between the foreground jaws while the upper gripper has shifted around it. The white cap still appears seated, with no clear loosening or removal to establish further progress.
